Thanks Liam — great next steps. Short answers up front, then a proposed technical handoff agenda and timeline.

Recommended model flavors (first-pass):
- Red-FT-13B-v2 (38-bit quantized): good quality/cost balance for structured extraction and tool calls.
- LlamaX-70B-q4: higher quality for edge cases (long context/gap-fill) — fallback for critical items.
- Red-Embed-2k: embeddings for semantic search + deduping of similar records.

Benchmarks & acceptance targets (proposal):
- Schema compliance (JSON strict): >= 95% pass on test set.
- Structural hallucination target: < 1% where an entity is fabricated.
- Latency SLO: p50 <= 220ms for 512-token generation on Dedicated pool.
- Cost target: gross token unit < $0.003 with prefix caching enabled.

How we validate JSON schema & retries (summary):
- Redwood Optimize runs a test harness that validates payloads against your JSON schema using strict type checks + enum enforcement.
- For function/tool calls we run a three-attempt retry policy with exponential backoff (250ms -> 750ms -> 2s) and circuit-breaker for repeated schema failures.
- We include structured unit tests: schema-only checks, end-to-end generation + post-parse validation, and synthetic adversarial prompts to probe hallucination.

Proposed handoff call (30–45 min):
1) Tech contact + scope (we'll invite Dylan and Ben for inference sizing + eval design)
2) Share sanitized sample & JSON schemas (you upload to Drive link)
3) Define 3-week pilot: initial sweep (1k examples) -> tweak prompts -> full 10k sample run -> results review
4) Acceptance gates and roll/fallback plan

Attachments: prompt-set template and a small sample harness we use for async runs.

[Attachment: ember_promptset_v1.json (6 KB)]

Do any of these targets feel off? If not, I'll schedule the handoff for early next week and share a concrete evaluation plan.

Looping in the evaluation strategy and a few technical notes. Monica — feel free to copy the below into the plan doc.

Evaluation strategy (technical):
- Phase 0 (sanity): run the promptset (ember_promptset_v1.json) against Red-FT-13B-v2 on a small infra profile to get warm KV cache metrics. Expect 10–15% improvement once prefix caching is active.
- Phase 1 (sweep): 1k anonymized examples across the main templates. Metrics: schema pass rate, field-level precision/recall for mapping labels, and hallucination rate (manual spot-check on 5%).
- Phase 2 (stress): 10k run with LlamaX-70B-q4 as a comparison on a subset (2k). Measure tail latency and cost delta.

Tool/function calling & retries:
- We instrument the runtime to emit a per-call envelope: request_id, model_variant, kv_cache_hit, attempts, parse_error (if any). Those go into the Console traces and are surfaced on per-route dashboards.
- For JSON schema failures we capture the raw output and the post-parse error to aid prompt tuning; we also run a small repair pass for non-critical structural issues (e.g., missing optional fields) before counting as fail — repair rules are configurable.

Deliverables we'll provide within the pilot:
- Benchmarks CSV (seen attached) with per-example outputs, parse flags, and scoring.
- A prompt cookbook with slot-based templates for constrained generation.
- A suggested retry & repair config for your production route.

I'll schedule the handoff slot for Mon 2028-03-27 10:00 PT if that works. Ben — can you estimate Dedicated footprint for the initial 2k preview and the 10k run?

—Dylan
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

- For LlamaX-70B-q4 sampling (2k subset) use burst on Hosted with throttles; estimated incremental cost: ~$2,300.
